name: Reference implementation recipe clone boundary
decision: KRN may lab-test reviewed reference implementations as executable recipes for repeated code patterns when the exemplar is local, versioned, source-to-decision mapped, covered by verification evidence, and paired with a falsifier. The exemplar can guide future implementation shape, but it must not replace tests, review gates, evidence capture, or proof/non-proof boundaries.
sourceRefs: user-provided screenshots 2026-07-01: reference implementation, clone workflow, recipe hashing, and code-as-up-to-date-documentation practitioner notes
falsifier: A future KRN slice can treat an example file or clone recipe as authoritative without local verification evidence, source-to-decision mapping, version or drift evidence, reviewability reasons, or proof/non-proof boundaries while brain-knowledge readback still marks the pattern ready.
doesNotProve: This pattern does not prove clone workflows outperform skills, that public practitioner sources are correct, that paid or proprietary course material may be copied, that generated code should bypass review, or that KRN should add a broad skill, subagent, crawler, or recipe runtime system now.
